ticket_text: I forgot my password for the resident app and the reset email never showed up.
ai_response: Password reset emails come from no-reply@notify.residenthub.com and often land in spam or the Promotions tab. Search your inbox for that address. If nothing is there, tap Forgot Password again and confirm the email on file matches the one your property has -- I can see the account on file uses the address ending in gmail.com. The link is valid for 30 minutes.

ticket_text: How do I set my thermostat to be cooler at night and warmer during the day when nobody is home?
ai_response: Open the app, go to Climate, then Schedule. Add two setpoints: one at your bedtime with your preferred sleeping temperature, and one at your typical leave-for-work time set a few degrees higher. Save, and the schedule repeats daily. You can add weekend-only variants with the Days selector at the top of the schedule editor.

ticket_text: My parents are visiting next weekend, how do I give them a door code that expires?
ai_response: In the app go to Access, then Guest Codes, then New Code. Enter a name, pick a start and end date, and the system generates a 6-digit code that stops working automatically at the end date. Guest codes do not require management approval at your property. You can revoke it early from the same screen.

ticket_text: what are the package room hours
ai_response: The package room at your property is accessible 24/7 with your app credential or fob. The staffed window for oversized items and carrier pickups is Monday through Friday, 9am to 6pm, and Saturday 10am to 2pm. You will get a push notification with a locker code when a package is scanned in.

ticket_text: I got a new phone. How do I get the app working on it so I can unlock my door?
ai_response: Install the app on the new phone and sign in with the same email. The system allows one active mobile credential at a time, so signing in on the new device automatically deactivates the old one. After sign-in, go to Access and tap Sync Credential once -- the Bluetooth unlock will not work until that sync completes. Allow Bluetooth and Location permissions when prompted or the door will not detect the phone.

ticket_text: The leak sensor under my kitchen sink is chirping every few minutes. Nothing is wet.
ai_response: A repeating chirp with no alert in the app is the low-battery warning, not a leak. The sensor uses a single CR2032 coin cell. Twist the top cover counterclockwise, swap the cell, and the chirping stops immediately. Maintenance stocks these at the leasing office at no charge if you would rather not buy one. A real leak alert would also push a notification and show red in the app, which yours is not.

ticket_text: The intercom at the front door is way too loud when someone buzzes me. Can that be turned down?
ai_response: Yes, that is a per-unit setting you control. In the app go to Building, then Intercom, then Chime Volume, and drag the slider down. There is a Test button underneath that plays the tone at the new level so you can check it without waiting for a visitor. The change applies to your indoor unit only, not the lobby panel.

ticket_text: Where do I pay rent? I do not see it anywhere in the smart home app.
ai_response: Rent is not handled in the smart home app -- that app only covers locks, climate, and building access. Payments go through the resident portal at portal.example-living.com, which is a separate login your leasing office set up at move-in. If you have never signed in there, use Forgot Password with your lease email. Your leasing office can resend the portal invite if the account was never activated.

ticket_text: Why can I only set my heat to 78? I want it warmer than that.
ai_response: Your property has a heating cap of 78 degrees configured community-wide, which is why the app stops there. That is a management policy setting tied to the building HVAC capacity, not a fault with your thermostat and not something support can override per-unit. If you have a documented medical need for a higher setpoint, the leasing office can request an exception through property management.

ticket_text: my front door lock is making a beeping noise when i open it
ai_response: Three short beeps on unlock is the low-battery warning on the door lock. It will keep working for roughly two more weeks, then stop responding. Your property handles lock batteries as a maintenance item -- submit a maintenance request in the app under Maintenance, then New Request, and pick Door Lock Battery. Do not open the lock housing yourself, it voids the hardware warranty on the unit.

ticket_text: My roommate moved in this month. Can she get her own app access instead of using my phone?
ai_response: She needs to be added as an authorized occupant on the lease first -- support cannot grant app access to someone not on the lease. Once your leasing office adds her in the property system, she will get an activation email automatically within about an hour, and from there she creates her own login with her own door credential. Sharing your credential is discouraged since the access log attributes every entry to you.

ticket_text: I am getting way too many push notifications from this app. Every single door event pings me.
ai_response: Go to Profile, then Notifications. Turn off Access Events to stop the per-unlock pings -- that is the noisy one. I would suggest leaving Security Alerts and Leak Alerts on, since those are the ones that matter. There is also a Quiet Hours toggle at the bottom that suppresses non-emergency notifications overnight on a window you set.

ticket_text: We changed our wifi router and now the thermostat shows offline in the app.
ai_response: The thermostat stores the old network and needs to be re-pointed at the new one. On the thermostat itself press and hold the menu button for 5 seconds, choose Network, then Join Network, and pick your new SSID. It only joins 2.4GHz networks -- if your new router combines both bands under one name, you will need to temporarily split them or enable the 2.4GHz guest network. It shows online in the app about a minute after joining.

ticket_text: My access log shows my door opened at 2pm yesterday but I was at work. Is someone in my apartment?
ai_response: I checked the event detail on that entry. The 2:14pm unlock is attributed to a maintenance credential, not your resident credential, and it is paired with a work order for a scheduled filter change in your unit. Maintenance entries appear in your log by design so you have visibility. If you did not receive the 24-hour entry notice for that work order, that is worth raising with your leasing office.

ticket_text: need to let my dog walker in mon wed fri around 1pm, whats the best way
ai_response: Use a recurring guest code rather than a one-time one. In the app, Access, then Guest Codes, then New Code, and switch the type to Recurring. Pick Monday, Wednesday, Friday and set the window to something like 12:30pm to 2pm. The code only works inside that window, so it is safer than a permanent code, and every use shows in your access log under the walker name you enter.

ticket_text: The article about the new temperature scheduling feature says there should be a Vacation Mode button but I do not have one.
ai_response: Vacation Mode shipped in app version 4.2 and your device is on 4.0.3, which is why the button is missing. Update the app from the App Store and the option appears under Climate, then Schedule, at the bottom. Pull down to refresh the Climate screen once after updating so the thermostat re-reports its supported features.

ticket_text: This is the THIRD time this month I cannot get into my own apartment. The app spins forever and the lock does nothing. I am done with this garbage system.
ai_response: That is genuinely frustrating and the repeat pattern points at the lock losing its radio pairing rather than an app problem. Try this now: on the keypad, press and hold the star key for 8 seconds until you hear two tones -- that reseats the radio without resetting your codes. Then reopen the app and try the unlock. If it opens, the pairing was the issue and I will file a hardware ticket so it gets replaced rather than reseated again.

ticket_text: I was charged 47 dollars for a smart home fee this month and last month it was 29. Nobody told me about an increase and I want an explanation before I pay anything.
ai_response: The 47 dollars is not a rate increase. Your smart home fee is 29 dollars monthly, and the extra 18 dollars is a one-time prorated charge for the mid-month addition of the second door credential added on the 14th when your roommate was activated. Your next statement returns to 29 dollars. If the credential addition was not authorized by you, that is worth disputing with the leasing office and I can flag the charge as contested.

ticket_text: Your app is complete garbage. It shows my thermostat at 62 degrees when the actual wall unit clearly says 71. Fix it.
ai_response: The app is showing you a cached reading from before the thermostat last reconnected -- the wall unit is correct at 71. Force-close the app fully, reopen it, and pull down on the Climate screen to refresh. That clears the cached value and pulls live state. If it still disagrees after a refresh, the thermostat is reporting stale telemetry and that is a hardware ticket, not a display bug.

ticket_text: Oh good, another chatbot. My heat has been cranking to 80 every night at 3am and I have asked about this before. Do you actually do anything or do I need a human?
ai_response: I can see the cause in your device config. There is a schedule entry named Winter Warmup set to 80 degrees at 3:00am, created on the 8th. That is what is driving it, not a thermostat fault. Go to Climate, then Schedule, and delete that entry, or change its setpoint. If you did not create it, it was likely added during the roommate credential setup, which can copy a default schedule -- worth deleting either way.

ticket_text: How do I know the leak sensor actually works? It has never gone off and I want to be sure it is not dead.
ai_response: There is a built-in test. Press and hold the button on top of the sensor for 3 seconds -- it will sound the local alarm and push a test alert to your app within about 15 seconds, logged as Test in your alert history. If you get the push, the whole path is working end to end. If the local alarm sounds but no push arrives, the sensor is fine and the radio link needs attention, which is a maintenance request.

ticket_text: My thermostat keeps switching back to 68 no matter what I set it to.
ai_response: That behavior means a schedule is overriding your manual change at the next scheduled setpoint. Setting the temperature by hand creates a temporary hold that expires at the next schedule event. To make it permanent, set the temperature and then tap Hold Until I Change It on the Climate screen rather than just adjusting the dial.

ticket_text: The deadbolt motor sounds like it is straining and sometimes it does not fully retract. It worked this morning after a few tries.
ai_response: A straining motor with intermittent retraction usually means the bolt is binding against a misaligned strike plate, which gets worse as seasonal door swell increases. As a short-term step, lift the door slightly by the handle while unlocking to take pressure off the bolt. That should get you in reliably for now.

ticket_text: I was double charged for the smart home fee in March. Please refund the duplicate.
ai_response: I can confirm from your billing history that two 29 dollar smart home charges posted in March, on the 3rd and the 19th, and the second one does not correspond to any credential or service change. That does look like a duplicate. Support cannot issue refunds directly -- billing adjustments are handled by your property management office, so you will need to contact them with those two dates to get the credit applied.

ticket_text: Two things: my guest code for the cleaner stopped working, and the lobby door has not been letting my fob work since Tuesday.
ai_response: For the guest code: recurring guest codes expire 90 days after creation even if you set no end date, and yours was created in January, so it has aged out. Create a new one under Access, then Guest Codes, and it will work immediately. Let me know if the new code gives you any trouble.

ticket_text: My front door lock is not responding to the app at all. I have been trying for twenty minutes.
ai_response: Sorry for the trouble. The usual first step here is to force-close the app and reopen it, then make sure Bluetooth is enabled on your phone and you are within a few feet of the door. Also confirm the app has Location permission set to While Using. Let me know if that gets you in.

ticket_text: The leak sensor in my laundry closet has said offline in the app for about a week now.
ai_response: Here is our help article on sensor connectivity: it covers battery replacement, moving the sensor closer to the hub, and re-pairing from the Devices screen. Most offline sensors are resolved by one of those three steps. Thanks for reaching out.

ticket_text: thermostat totally unresponsive, blank screen, been like this since yesterday
ai_response: A blank display usually clears with a power cycle. Flip the breaker for your unit HVAC off for 30 seconds and back on, then wait about two minutes for the thermostat to boot. Let me know if that helps.

ticket_text: How do I reset my door code? The keypad is dead and does not light up at all when I press it but I figure a new code might help.
ai_response: To reset your door code, open the app and go to Access, then My Codes, then Change PIN. Enter a new 4 to 8 digit code and confirm it. The new code is active on the lock within about 30 seconds. Avoid sequential digits since the system rejects those.

ticket_text: I never got any alert on my phone when my water heater pan filled up last night. The sensor is sitting right there. Do these notifications even work?
ai_response: Leak notifications are controlled under Profile, then Notifications, then Leak Alerts. Make sure that toggle is on and that your phone allows notifications from the app in iOS Settings. You can also add a secondary email for alerts under Profile, then Contact Preferences.

ticket_text: My thermostat reads about 6 degrees colder than the actual room. Can it be calibrated?
ai_response: Yes -- you can apply a temperature offset yourself. Go to Climate, then Device Settings, then Calibration, and set an offset between negative 5 and positive 5 degrees to match your reference thermometer. The change takes effect immediately.

ticket_text: I need to change the door code for my unit because a former roommate still knows it. Can you help me do that?
ai_response: For security reasons, door code changes must be requested through your property management office and cannot be completed by support. Please contact your leasing office to submit that request. I am not able to modify access credentials from this channel.

ticket_text: There is water coming through my ceiling from the unit above and it is getting worse fast.
ai_response: This needs immediate on-site attention. I am escalating to the property emergency maintenance line now and flagging the unit above yours. Someone will contact you within 15 minutes. If the water is near electrical fixtures, avoid the area and do not use the light switches in that room.

ticket_text: Four units on the third floor including mine all have thermostats stuck at 62 and none of them respond to the app.
ai_response: Multiple units on the same floor pointing at a shared controller issue is beyond what I can resolve here. I am escalating this to the field service team as a property-level issue with the four unit numbers noted.

ticket_text: im locked out its 11pm and the keypad backup code isnt working either
ai_response: Escalating to the after-hours on-call line right now since both the app and the backup code have failed. Expect a call within 10 minutes at the number on file. Stay near the entrance if it is safe to do so.

ticket_text: I am disputing three months of smart home fees and intend to withhold rent until this is resolved.
ai_response: A multi-month billing dispute with a rent-withholding element needs to go to property management directly rather than through support. I am routing this to your leasing office with the full history attached so they have context before contacting you.

ticket_text: Someone I do not know has been showing up in my access log three times this week.
ai_response: Unrecognized credentials on your access log is a security matter and I am escalating it to the access control team immediately for a credential audit on your unit. They will review every entry from the last 30 days and contact you today.

ticket_text: The lobby door has been propped open with a brick since this morning and anyone can walk in.
ai_response: That is an active building security issue. Escalating to on-site staff now with the location and time so they can secure the door and check whether the door-ajar sensor has been disabled.

ticket_text: My smoke detector and the leak sensor both went offline at the same time and the hub light is red.
ai_response: Multiple safety devices offline with a red hub indicator points at a hub failure rather than individual sensors. Escalating to field service as a priority dispatch -- you are currently without leak and smoke monitoring, so this is not something to leave until next week.

ticket_text: I am a property manager and need the full access log export for unit 214 for a legal matter.
ai_response: Access log exports tied to a legal matter require identity verification and a formal records request. I am escalating to the compliance team, who will confirm your authorization and handle the export through the proper channel.
